g.text: S
SITUATION
"Kofi, 4, shock?"
B
BACKGROUND
"diarrhoea, day 2"
A
ASSESSMENT
"weak pulse…"
R
RECOMMEND.
"come + IV now!"
SBAR (exam pure!): Situation (who + what's wrong NOW!) · Background (admission +
course!) · Assessment (YOUR findings + worry!) · Recommendation (what you NEED!). 60
seconds, spoken + read-back. ISBAR adds I (Identify: "Ama, RN, ward B"!).
READ-BACK (closed loop!): every order + critical value repeated ("insulin 8 units —
confirm?") + confirmed ("confirmed!"). No read-back = open loop = error hunting ground.
BEDSIDE HANDOVER: at the bed + patient included ("anything to add, Maame?") + charts +
pumps checked TOGETHER. Catches errors (wrong fluids! missed doses!), builds trust, teaches
juniors. Sensitive news aside first — dignity before process.
STRUCTURED TOOLS: written handover sheets (same headings every shift!) · EHR summaries ·
whiteboards (allergies! falls! NPO!) · safety huddles (5-min start-of-shift: "who's sickest?
what's pending?"). Memory-only handover = malpractice invitation.
ESCALATION (CUS!): "I'm CONCERNED… I'm UNCOMFORTABLE… this is a SAFETY issue!" — rising
assertiveness + chain of command (senior → doctor → matron → medical director). Silence
kills: unvoiced worry is unwitnessed harm (PRO-I compass!). Document escalations.
INTERPROFESSIONAL: first names + roles + respect ("doctor, 60 seconds?") · pharmacist/
physio/dietician consulted EARLY · ward rounds: nurse presents (you know MOST!) · disagree
privately, unite publicly. Hierarchy never outranks safety.
PHONE SBAR: identify + SBAR + read-back + "when will you come? what meanwhile?" + NAME
taken + documented. Night calls concise: situation FIRST, never story-first.
LINKS: INF M02 downtime/handover · PRO-I M5/M6 · GER M6 · NUT M6 referrals.
MANTRA: "SBAR it, read it back, bedside it, escalate it."
